source.title: Soteria: Language-Specific Functional Parameter Steering for Multilingual Safety Alignment
source.authors: Somnath Banerjee; Sayan Layek; Pratyush Chatterjee; Animesh Mukherjee; Rima Hazra

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present, though some tables are flattened in extraction.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether a parameter-targeted intervention can change harmful-output rates, using functional-head selection and harm-vector subtraction rather than the fine-tuning or token-position methods in the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper fine-tunes a harmful model to derive a harm vector, but reports no harmful-compliance result for that fine-tuned model, so this is not evidence for V1. It does not measure per-token KL, prefilling, or safety training depth. Rows cover the reported Soteria safety outcomes, its random-head comparison, head-percentage sweep, and jailbreak results.
record.test_reason: Soteria is a safety-restoration method. It subtracts a harm vector (harmful fine-tuned model minus target) restricted to the O-projection blocks of selected attention heads, then reports how much ASR drops. Every result measures the study's own mitigation against the untreated model, random heads, or other defenses. None measures whether safety training is shallow. The study never reports harmful compliance of its harmful fine-tuned model (V1). It never measures per-token KL (V3) or prefill, suffix or decoding attacks (V4). It does not test whether removing or ablating a small weight set disables safety (V5). Lowering ASR by editing about 3% of parameters is a mitigation result, not evidence that safety lives in those parameters.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also claim Soteria beats Safety Arithmetic, Resta and TIES, and is robust to POATE and refusal-direction jailbreaks. Their own text concedes that reductions in low-resource languages remain limited.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a harmful-model-minus-target-model harm vector, masks it to selected language-specific attention-head O-projection blocks, and subtracts the masked vector; it is not fine-tuning the aligned model on small harmful or benign datasets.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes vary by dataset, language resource level, model, and percentage of heads retained. The paper also reports differences between selected and random attention heads.

fits_no_version.finding: Subtracting a harm vector restricted to O-projection blocks of task-selected heads (~3% of parameters) lowers ASR more than random heads. Examples on MultiJail high-resource: Llama 0.42→0.19 vs random 0.32; Qwen 0.24→0.11 vs 0.21. MMLU is unchanged.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety can be restored by editing a small, selected subset of attention-head output weights (mitigation-side localization).

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the safety rates. The paper says some language-specific head selection may be less precise because of limited resources, training data, script variation, or morphology. Some tables are flattened in the supplied text. The attack evaluation reports attack ASRs and Soteria comparisons, but no per-token or compliant-opening test.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports additional base-versus-Soteria safety results in Figure 3, Figure 4, Table 1, Table 4, and Table 5, including many model-by-language-by-dataset cells. These were left out to stay within the 60-row limit and avoid duplicating the benchmark outcomes represented in Table 7 and the attack and head-percentage results. The utility benchmarks in Table 2 do not measure the claim’s safety behaviour and were not included.

untested.parts: A harmful model is fine-tuned (up to 1000 harmful QA samples, 3 epochs) only to build the harm vector; its harmful compliance rate is never reported.
No per-token KL or position analysis.
No prefill, suffix or decoding attacks; POATE/RDR are used only to stress the defense.
No ablation showing that removing a small weight set disables safety; edits are additive safety steering.
No training that deepens safety across tokens.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4 and V5 labels are dropped. The V4 labels cited rows not linked to V4. Both sets of labels rest on the study's own mitigation performance, which per the rules is T4, not a test. The 'LLaMA' subject in Table 7 is llama3.1-8b-instruct, and the '8B model' rows are also Llama 3.1 8B Instruct. The study cites Qi et al. 2023 (an original source) only for the harm taxonomy and ASR metric.

versions.untested_parts: No harmful fine-tuning compliance rate is reported for the harmful model used to form the harm vector.
No per-token KL divergence or aligned-versus-base output-distribution comparison is measured.
Tests POATE and refusal-direction-removal (RDR) jailbreak attacks, but not compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes as such, or decoding changes.
Tests steering through selected attention-head O-projection weights and a heads-percentage sweep; does not establish that a small set of weights or ranks uniquely carries safety behaviour.
Does not compare training data or objectives as causes of shallow safety.
Does not train safety to be deeper across response tokens or test its persistence.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: POATE and RDR attacks on the evaluated Llama 3.1 8B settings
reader_labels.reason: The reported attack ASRs remain nonzero after Soteria across datasets and resource levels, consistent with attacks eliciting harmful outputs; see r25-r36.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: POATE and RDR with Soteria applied
reader_labels.reason: Soteria lowers the reported attack ASRs compared with Base-J in all listed settings, so these results do not show attacks defeating safety without qualification; see r25-r36.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Selected-head Soteria interventions in the Table 7 benchmark settings
reader_labels.reason: Changing selected functional-head weights is followed by lower ASR than the base model in most reported settings; see r01-r10 and r12.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Soteria has no reported reduction for Qwen on low-resource XThreatBench, and random-head selection also lowers ASR in multiple settings; the results do not show that safety is exclusively localized to the selected heads; see r11, r13-r24.
